correctness.rationale: Exactly the nonempty first-site-vacant states T have reset edges, and every such edge leaves T. Finite stationary tree polynomials have degree at most |T|. A degree-|T| in-tree rooted at the singleton e1 exists: choose one reset from each T, advance and remove the rightmost downstream particle from occupied-first-site states without disturbing site 1, and inject from empty. Each slow step in an occupied-first-site state strictly decreases the sum of downstream distances to removal. Roots in T lose one possible reset factor; with any other root, including empty, selecting all reset factors forces the disallowed e1 to z2 to e1 two-cycle. Normalization therefore gives pi(e1)=1+O(1/r) and other masses O(1/r). No reset enters T, and the only O(1) ordinary inflow from e1 is to z2, whose reset rate is r. Thus pi(z2)=1/r+O(1/r^2) and other T masses are O(1/r^2). The empty probability is beta/alpha times pi(z_L), contributing at order 1/r if and only if L=2. Stationary particle-count conservation gives both extraction and injection currents, including the stated coefficients and remainders. Independently `python /workspace/branches/audit_checks.py reset` solves the finite Poisson equation for the stationary extraction rate at symbolic L=2 and at L=3,4 with alpha=2,beta=3; it confirms both leading branches. The frozen diagnostic was inspected, not executed. No estimate uniform in growing L or vanishing boundary rates follows.
